title: Calculating A BRUTAL Bishop Sac | Smith–Morra Gambit | The Sensei Speedrun | GM Naroditsky

moves.spoken: Facing an eighteen-eighty-something. e4, c5 — and another Smith-Morra, just like the last game started; let's hope for a different result.
d4, throwing the pawn into the fray.
Black grabs it, c takes d4.
c3 — the true Smith-Morra, offering a second pawn for a big lead in development.
Black accepts with d takes c3, and we recapture, the knight to c3 — a fully accepted Morra.
Black plays e6. The guideline here is that you generally want the knight to f3 before the bishop to c4 in most of these positions.
So we develop the knight to f3 first, staying as flexible as possible and waiting for Black to commit to a setup before we do.
Black plays a6, heading into a main-line structure.
Now the bishop to c4 — you don't want it drifting to f4 where the e5-break could hit it with tempo. On c4 it's perfectly placed.
Black develops the bishop to e7. Our bishop on c4 is what makes the position tick — it quietly supports the knight that later jumps to d5.
We castle, tucking the king away and finishing development ahead of schedule.
And remember: after our knight eventually lands on d5, Black is not obliged to take it — that tension is part of what gives White the initiative.
Black plays d6, essentially transposing into a line I'm quite comfortable against.
You have to trust that this gambit lead eventually creates an impact — and it did; a nice game.
